products.name: Miro
products.description: Enterprise-scale visual collaboration workspace with infinite canvas, real-time multi-user support (500+ concurrent), AI features (clustering, summarization, workflows), unlimited boards, and 500+ integrations across Jira, Slack, Asana, Salesforce, Zapier
products.positioning: Innovation workspace for cross-functional teams, from brainstorming to delivery

products.name: FigJam
products.description: Lightweight collaborative whiteboard integrated into Figma design ecosystem. Features 300+ templates, sticky notes, voting, timers, real-time collaboration, open-session guest access (24-hour no-login links), and AI-assisted ideation. Positioned as Figma's whiteboarding solution for design teams and early-stage ideation.
products.positioning: Frictionless whiteboarding for design teams, seamlessly integrated with Figma design workflow

products.name: Mural
products.description: Facilitation-first visual collaboration platform optimized for structured workshops. Features include real-time collaboration, LUMA frameworks integration, private/confidential workspace modes, timer and voting tools, enterprise controls (SSO, SCIM, 2FA, data residency, BYOK), and unlimited external guest collaboration.
products.positioning: Enterprise visual collaboration platform with facilitation-led workflow support and strong governance controls

products.name: Excalidraw
products.description: Free, open-source (MIT license) web-based whiteboard focused on simplicity and privacy. Hand-drawn aesthetic, real-time collaboration via shareable links, end-to-end encryption, progressive web app (offline support), no account required, and library of ready-to-use sketches. Trusted by large enterprises and developers.
products.positioning: Simple, private, open-source whiteboard for sketching, collaboration, and diagramming without vendor lock-in

products.name: tldraw
products.description: Open-source (MIT) infinite canvas whiteboard with React SDK for embedding. Features geometric shapes, connectors, real-time collaboration, professional aesthetic, and developer-friendly architecture. Free web version; commercial SDK licensing $6000/year for production use. 45k+ GitHub stars, active developer community adoption.
products.positioning: Infinite canvas whiteboard and React SDK for developers, with professional aesthetic and real-time collaboration

products.name: Whimsical
products.description: Lightweight visual workspace supporting flowcharts, wireframes, mind maps, and Kanban boards on infinite canvas. Features real-time collaboration, 300+ templates, version history (7-90 days based on plan), password-protected sharing, and admin controls. Positioned as the more accessible Miro alternative for smaller teams with lower learning curve.
products.positioning: Lightweight multi-format visual workspace for smaller teams and simpler workflows

products.name: Napkin AI
products.description: AI-powered text-to-diagram tool for rapid visual prototyping. Supports 30+ diagram types auto-generated from natural language. Features include wireframe-to-code generation, unlimited visual editing on AI outputs, content generation (text, images, data tables), and AI credit system (500 credits/week free, 10k-30k/month paid plans).
products.positioning: AI-first diagram generation platform enabling teams to prototype visuals and code from plain text descriptions

products.name: Qlerify
products.description: AI-powered visual modeling platform specialized in Domain-Driven Design (DDD) methodology. Supports Event Storming, CQRS patterns, process mapping, and code generation from domain models. Targets architects and teams formalizing domain understanding before development.
products.positioning: AI-powered domain-driven design platform enabling teams to model business domains and generate code

products.name: MockFlow
products.description: UI/wireframing and rapid prototyping platform for product designers and UX teams. Includes WireframePro, Product Design Suite, SiteMap tools, code generation (React, Tailwind, Shadcn, iOS, Kotlin), AI-powered wireframe/sitemap generation, and team review/feedback tools. Designed for design-centric workflows.
products.positioning: UI/wireframing and rapid prototyping platform enabling design teams to translate ideas into interactive mockups and code

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Miro dominates infinite-canvas whiteboards with strongest AI and integrations, but lacks graph semantics forcing manual organization. MetroGraph provides queryable graphs with automatic ER/relationship discovery, reducing cognitive load on complex data. For teams dealing with database schemas or multi-entity systems, MetroGraph eliminates the sticky-note sprawl plaguing Miro workflows.
they_win_on: market scale ($17.6B valuation, 476M+ raised)
team collaboration at massive scale (500+ concurrent users verified)
extensive template library (1000+ templates)
deepest integration ecosystem (500+ integrations: Jira, Slack, Asana, Salesforce, Zapier)
AI-powered workspace features (clustering, summarization, Miro Workflows)
enterprise governance (Enterprise Guard, SCIM, audit logs)
established market dominance (4.7/5 Capterra rating)
we_win_on: queryable data visualization (actual results, not freeform sketches)
graph structure preservation (no context loss on infinite canvas)
schema introspection (auto-generated ER from live databases)
reduced surface area (focused on data teams, not all-purpose collaboration)
AI + UI parity (copilot doesn't steal focus from graph)
competitors.moat: Dominant market position with $17.6B valuation, 500+ integration ecosystem, massive user network effects in design/product/agile communities

competitors.wedge_vs_them: FigJam wins on design-team simplicity and frictionless Figma integration, optimized for ideation sessions not data systems. MetroGraph targets data engineers and noSQL/SQL startups where Figma's design-first UX creates friction. FigJam's strength (design toolchain alignment) irrelevant for database visualization; MetroGraph advantage (queryable schema + live data binding) invisible in design workflows.
they_win_on: Figma ecosystem lock-in (300M+ design tool users)
24-hour guest access without login (world's lowest entry barrier)
simplicity for early-stage ideation (lower surface area than Miro)
tight design-to-dev handoff workflow (Figma platform integration)
IPO liquidity and brand strength (July 2025 at $17.6-18.8B valuation)
developer seat pricing ($3-12/month collab seats)
we_win_on: reduced need for templates (auto-generated from data)
SQL/noSQL team adoption (not design team focus)
competitors.moat: Figma ecosystem dominance in design tools, 749M+ total funding, IPO momentum in design community

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Mural differentiates on facilitation-first workflows and enterprise controls, but suffers same infinite-canvas problems as Miro for data-heavy use cases. Stronger in regulated/structured workshops; MetroGraph stronger when users need persistent, queryable, semantically-rich artifacts. Teams doing data modeling or agent-graph building prefer MetroGraph's structure over Mural's facilitation-optimized flexibility.
they_win_on: facilitation-led workshop templates (timers, voting, breakout rooms)
enterprise security depth (SSO, SCIM, 2FA, data residency, BYOK)
LUMA frameworks integration (enterprise methodology)
private + confidential room modes (regulated industries)
dedicated support tier and transformation expertise
competitors.moat: Enterprise facilitation methodology positioning, established practices in regulated industries and consulting firms

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Excalidraw is free, privacy-first alternative winning on simplicity and no-account friction, but purely freeform with zero data binding. MetroGraph can't compete on free/open-source, but solves different problem: queryable structure. Excalidraw users needing persistence upgrade to Miro; they don't upgrade to MetroGraph unless they have database visualization needs.

competitors.moat: Open-source community, privacy-first positioning, zero sign-up barrier

Markets adjacent, non-overlapping—unless MetroGraph embeds as tldraw's data visualization backend.

Different use cases—though some overlap in users needing both text-to-code (Napkin) and data-to-graph (MetroGraph).

Qlerify wins for architecture teams doing formal DDD; MetroGraph wins for data teams doing ER/workflow visualization. Could be complementary—Qlerify models visualizable in MetroGraph.

notes: Phase C extraction for competitors-diagramming-whiteboard leaf. Market scope: 9 products in focus (Miro, FigJam, Excalidraw, tldraw, Whimsical, Napkin, Qlerify, Mural, MockFlow) plus extended competitive set (Lucidchart, draw.io, Conceptboard, AFFiNE, Boardmix, Microsoft Whiteboard). Sources: 70 curated sources (T0 official, T1 technical, T2 reviews/analysts, T3 practitioner analysis). Positioning: MetroGraph = queryable graph visualization for noSQL/SQL teams; Whiteboards = infinite-canvas ideation (no data binding). Direct threat from Miro/FigJam/Mural (same canvas model, broader market); Adjacent from Napkin/Whimsical/Excalidraw/tldraw (different value prop); Indirect from Qlerify (DDD-specific); Low threat from MockFlow (design-focused). Feature differentiation: MetroGraph wins on schema introspection, query-driven updates, data binding; Whiteboards win on accessibility (no DB knowledge), scale (500+ users), template libraries, ecosystems. HCI note: Whiteboards suffer surface-area bloat and AI-sidebar flight (users give up on UI for chat); MetroGraph solves via graph semantics and AI+UI parity.
